question_verdicts.reason: The value at IOBoard.md:338 is an assumption (marking 6), and every assumption is a question to the owner (P1 row, Research.md Agent layout). The answer decides whether the excitation is the rail itself or a part R13 selects, and which rail R5 sizes for it. It also bounds the bridge ADC's analogue supply. On the ADS1232 and ADS1234 seeds, AVDD is 2.7 to 5.3 V and VREF is at most AVDD + 0.1 V. A 5 V ratiometric excitation therefore needs AVDD between 5 and 5.3 V. Source: TI SBAS350H (revised June 2025), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1234.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z.

IOBoard.md:338 says 'The excitation and encoder currents are not stated'. R5 sizes the 5 V rail from the supply currents of the parts T2 and T4 select, plus the display's draw (Research.md:283, IOBoard.md:338). No round selects the load cells: the Scope table (Research.md:25-29) lists none, and the R13 row selects only the bridge ADC and excitation. So no P4 reports the cells' draw. Each cell draws 5 V divided by its bridge resistance. No bridge resistance appears anywhere in the checkout.

The checkout names no load cell and states no rated output. Rated output × 5 V gives each channel's full-scale input. It decides the gain a part needs. On the ADS123x seeds the PGA gives full-scale ranges of ±19.5 mV at gain 128 and ±39 mV at gain 64 (SBAS350H, read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z). Whether a cell's output fits one of them depends on this value.

A grep of the checkout finds no capacity for any cell. Capacity and rated output together turn a force step in N into a voltage step at the ADC input. Without the capacity, the resolution in N (question 5) cannot become a noise-free resolution in µV that P2 can check against a datasheet.

IOBoard.md:495 reads 'The thrust and torque ranges: not stated. F3's answer gives the channels and the excitation, not the ranges (R13).' The line itself assigns this missing value to R13. The sign matters: a part must read both polarities if thrust reverses or torque changes direction. Converting the torque range in N·m to force on each cell also needs the cells' distance from the axis. A critic addition asks for that distance.

Neither IOBoard.md nor Research.md states a resolution for thrust or torque (grep for thrust, torque and load cell, read 2026-09-28). With questions 2 and 3, the answer gives the step at the ADC input in µV, at the rate of question 7. That is the figure a bridge ADC's noise table is checked against.

No accuracy is stated for the load-cell channels. IOBoard.md:476 states accuracy as not stated only for the pack voltage and the motor current. Accuracy is one of the value kinds the P1 row lists (range, resolution, rate, accuracy). The answer bounds the gain, offset, nonlinearity and drift a part may have. The temperature span over which the drift counts is not stated either. A critic addition asks for it.

IOBoard.md:431 gives 20 ms sampling for the BENCH numbers, and no BENCH register carries thrust or torque (link_pages.h:229-244). No rate is stated for the load cells. A multiplexed part pays a settling delay on each channel change: SBAS350H section 7.3.7 gives a digital filter settling time of 4 conversions, with data rates of 10 or 80 SPS (read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z). So the rate per channel decides between one multiplexed part and one part per channel.

F3 (Research.md:531) takes torque from 2 cells, so the reading combines two channels. Neither page states how far apart in time the readings may be taken. The answer decides whether one multiplexed part is enough, like the 4-channel ADS1234 seed, or whether simultaneous or per-channel conversion is needed. That fixes placements per board, and so the need in the stock gate of sourcing rule 4 (need = boards × placements).

F3 gives only the channels and the excitation, and the checkout names no cell or wiring. On the ADS1232 and ADS1234 seeds, one REFP/REFN pair serves all 2 or 4 channels (pins 16/15 and 20/19; SBAS350H, read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z). So 3 six-wire cells whose sense leads each need a reference input do not fit one such part. P2 needs 4-wire or 6-wire to count the reference inputs.

added.question: At what distance from the motor axis, in mm, does each of the 2 torque cells take its load?
added.why: P1's question 4 asks the torque range in N·m, and questions 3 and 5 ask each cell's capacity and resolution in N. The force on a torque cell is the torque divided by its distance from the axis. Without that distance, P2 cannot turn the torque range into each torque cell's force range. It then cannot find the mV the channel's input spans or choose its gain. F3 (Research.md:531) says only 'torque on 2 cells', and neither page states where the cells sit.
added.for_quantity: torque cell distance from the motor axis

added.question: Over what ambient temperature range, in °C, must each load-cell channel hold the accuracy asked for it?
added.why: P1's question 6 asks an accuracy that counts drift with temperature. A datasheet gives drift per °C (ppm/°C, nV/°C), so the error it adds depends on the temperature span. The only range in the tree is 0 to 50 °C. It is stated for the monostable window (IOBoard.md:184) and the 3.3 V rail (Research.md:283), not for any measurement. Without the span, P2 cannot turn a part's drift figures into % of rated output.

added.question: What is the longest time, in ms, from a step change in thrust or torque to a fully settled reading on that channel?
added.why: A delta-sigma bridge ADC's digital filter delays a step by several conversions. On the ADS1232 and ADS1234 seeds, a fully settled reading after an input step takes 5 readings: 62.5 ms at 80 SPS and 500 ms at 10 SPS (TI SBAS350H, section 7.3.7 and the data-rate table, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1234.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z). The output rate of P1's question 7 does not bound this delay, because parts at the same rate differ in filter order. Neither page states a step response for thrust or torque.
added.for_quantity: load-cell settling time after a load step
